title: Depth bound after truncation
statement: Let $A$ be a finite set of coordinates and let $T$ be a binary decision tree whose leaves carry values in a type $\alpha$ and whose queries use coordinates from $A$, with each queried coordinate removed from the set available to its descendants. For any fallback value $a \in \alpha$ and any $k \in \mathbb{N}$, replacing each query reached when the remaining truncation parameter is zero by a leaf carrying $a$ produces a tree of depth at most $k$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite available set of coordinates
A decision tree over those coordinates with leaves in $\alpha$
